entry_thesis: The Strait of Hormuz closure is an ongoing, escalating supply shock with Iran's IRGC vowing zero oil passage — Brent approaching $100/b with structural supply tightness confirmed by today's EIA inventory report. However, upstream XLE is technically overbought (RSI ~76, broke upper Bollinger Band March 2, MACD negative since Feb 24) after a 22%+ YTD run, creating correction risk in the crowded trade. AMLP (Alerian MLP ETF) captures the same energy super-cycle thesis through fee-based midstream pipeline infrastructure — less commodity price sensitivity, 7.5% distribution yield, only 14% YTD vs XLE's 22%, with room to run as prolonged supply disruption drives throughput volumes and energy infrastructure becomes critical national-security infrastructure.
risk: A rapid diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict or ceasefire announcement would reduce energy throughput demand and compress MLP valuations, though fee-based revenue provides a structural floor vs. upstream producers.
catalyst: EIA weekly crude inventory report (March 6) expected to show accelerating supply draw; OPEC+ emergency response meeting; ongoing Hormuz closure driving record midstream throughput utilization as US domestic pipeline networks route around Persian Gulf disruption.

research_notes.treasury_yields: 10-year yield at 4.27-4.38% — rising yields compressing equity multiples, fee-based MLPs with yield support more resilient
research_notes.iran_hormuz: Crisis began Feb 28, 2026 — IRGC vowing 'not a litre of oil' through Hormuz. Brent approaching $100/b, 20% of global seaborne oil (20M bbl/day) disrupted by 90%+
research_notes.xle_overbought: XLE RSI ~76, broke upper Bollinger Band March 2, MACD turned negative Feb 24. Up 22%+ YTD — correction risk elevated after crowded run
research_notes.gold_rejected: Gold fell 6%+ to $5,085 on March 3 despite Iran conflict — dollar strength and bond yields dominating safe-haven flows. Gold thesis broken.
research_notes.amlp_thesis: AMLP up only ~14% YTD vs XLE 22% — relative value within energy. Fee-based pipeline revenues insulate from oil price volatility while still benefiting from supply disruption driving US domestic throughput. 7.5% trailing distribution yield provides downside cushion.
research_notes.thesis_evolution: Four consecutive energy/defense/gold picks — pivoting from upstream energy (XLE, overbought) to midstream infrastructure (AMLP) to capture same macro thesis at lower technical risk. Avoiding gold after March 3 breakdown.
